questions.q: In the set $Q^{+}$ of all positive rational numbers, the operation * is defined by the formula $a * b=\frac{a b}{6}$. Then, the inverse of 9 with respect
questions.solution:
Let $e$ be the identity.
$\begin{aligned}
& \therefore a * e=a \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{a b}{6}=a \\
& \Rightarrow e=6 \\
& \because a * a^{-1}=e \\
& \therefore a * a^{-1}=6 \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{a a^{-1}}{6}=6 \Rightarrow a^{-1}=\frac{6 \times 6}{a} \\
& \therefore 9^{-1}=\frac{6 \times 6}{9}=4
\end{aligned}$

questions.solution:
Clearly, $A$ is the set of all points on the circle $x^2+y^2=25$ and $B$ is the set of all points on the ellipse $x^2+9 y^2=144$. These two intersect at four points $P, Q, R$ and $S$.
Hence, $A \cap B$ contains four points.
